name: Bigin
tagline: Run a small-business pipeline with contacts, activities, and simple workflows

tiers.name: Express
tiers.limits: 50,000 records; no user-count limit (each user requires a license)

tiers.name: Premier
tiers.limits: 100,000 records; no user-count limit (each user requires a license)

tiers.name: Bigin 360
tiers.limits: 1,000,000 records; no user-count limit (each user requires a license)

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 user and 500 records total (contacts, companies, pipelines, activities, products and notes all count as records)
pricing.hiddenCosts: Local taxes may be added despite contradictory wording on the page; paid plans charge for every user. Add-ons are sold separately in the Bigin Store. Annual downgrades can create account credits rather than cash refunds.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Bigin, run a small-business pipeline with contacts, activities, and simple workflows. The hard boundary is zoho ecosystem, telephony, forms, integrations, and mobile apps, plus integrations, data quality, and workflow lock-in.
coreLoopDIY: Manage contacts and companies for a small business, move opportunities through a pipeline with simple workflows, log interactions and activities, and surface the next action.
whatYouLose: Zoho ecosystem, telephony, forms, integrations, and mobile apps
moatNotes: integrations, data quality, and workflow lock-in
ongoingBurden: deduplication, permissions, imports, sync, enrichment, email capture, automations, backups, and audit history
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Bigin because CRM value compounds as the system becomes the shared memory of every customer interaction and embeds itself in the rest of the stack. The recurring cost buys deduplication, permissions, imports, sync, enrichment, email capture, automations, backups, and audit history, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Twenty
priorArt.desc: Active open-source modern CRM with extensible data models.

alternatives.name: EspoCRM
alternatives.desc: A traditional CRM that actually lets you change the data model; polished enough, but still your server.

facts.install: Docker Compose or upload the PHP package and run the web installer
facts.dataFormat: CRM records in a self-hosted MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL database; uploaded files in server/Docker volumes
facts.gapVsPaid: EspoCRM is much heavier to configure and administer than Bigin’s deliberately simple small-business pipeline.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a server, database, domain/TLS setup, and ongoing upgrades/backups

alternatives.name: Frappe CRM
alternatives.desc: A clean leads-and-deals board with notes, tasks and email; Frappe underneath means a real server, not a toy.

facts.install: One-click Frappe Cloud signup or the official Python easy-install deployment script on your server
facts.dataFormat: CRM DocType records and attachments in the Frappe site database/files, on Frappe Cloud or the user's server
facts.gapVsPaid: Frappe CRM needs considerably more configuration to reach Bigin’s ready-made pipeline and workflow experience.
facts.setupBlocker: Free use means self-hosting; the official production script still needs a Linux server, DNS, and command-line access

alternatives.name: HubSpot Free CRM
alternatives.desc: A real two-seat CRM for free; 1,000 contacts is where the upsell starts counting.

facts.install: Hosted signup; optionally connect/import email, calendar, and contacts
facts.dataFormat: Structured CRM customer records stored and processed on HubSpot's cloud servers, with regional hosting options and exports
facts.gapVsPaid: HubSpot’s free tier puts much of the useful workflow automation behind paid hubs and surrounds the simple pipeline with a larger upsell-heavy suite.

alternatives.name: Krayin CRM
alternatives.desc: A Laravel sales pipeline with leads, contacts and email; glossy enough, but it still wants a PHP stack.

facts.install: Composer package, browser GUI installer, or Docker; managed cloud is also offered
facts.dataFormat: CRM records in MySQL/MariaDB (Laravel database); uploads in storage/app/public on the chosen host
facts.gapVsPaid: Krayin is less mature and less plug-and-play around everyday email, calendar, mobile, and workflow use than Bigin.
facts.setupBlocker: The free path requires PHP/Composer plus MySQL/MariaDB, or Docker and a server; HTTPS, backups, and updates remain yours

alternatives.name: Twenty
alternatives.desc: A modern pipeline CRM with custom objects, views and mailbox sync; the subscription becomes a Compose file.

facts.install: Hosted cloud signup or official one-line/Docker Compose self-host install
facts.dataFormat: CRM records and configuration in PostgreSQL; files in local storage or S3-compatible object storage on the selected host
facts.gapVsPaid: Twenty’s ready-made sales automation and small-business onboarding are thinner than Bigin’s out-of-the-box workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Free use requires Docker, at least 2 GB RAM, PostgreSQL-backed containers, secrets, and domain/TLS configuration

alternatives.name: Odoo CRM One App Free
alternatives.desc: A full hosted pipeline for unlimited users, provided CRM is the only Odoo app you marry.

facts.install: Hosted Odoo Online signup with CRM selected as the single free app
facts.dataFormat: Structured Odoo records in an Odoo-hosted customer database; records can be exported from list views
facts.gapVsPaid: Odoo is substantially more complex than Bigin, and the one-app-free bargain ends when the business needs another Odoo module.

alternatives.name: Zoho CRM Free
alternatives.desc: A full little CRM for three users and 5,000 records; the wider Zoho maze is optional.

facts.dataFormat: Structured CRM service data stored on Zoho's cloud servers; Zoho states users can access, export, and delete service data
facts.gapVsPaid: Zoho’s free plan is capped at three users and withholds the workflow automation depth that makes Bigin useful beyond a bare pipeline.

alternatives.name: Freshsales Free
alternatives.desc: A clean three-user pipeline with email and mobile apps; useful automation starts asking for rent.

facts.dataFormat: Structured CRM records and uploaded files stored in Freshworks' cloud; account data can be exported
facts.gapVsPaid: Freshsales Free covers a basic pipeline but withholds multiple pipelines, richer workflows, and sales sequences that Bigin users may rely on.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Express plan and a personal or very small-team CRM DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Bigin in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: manage contacts and companies for a small business, move opportunities through a pipeline with simple workflows, log interactions and activities, and surface the next action.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create contacts, companies, opportunities, notes, tasks, and configurable pipeline stages.
Add fast global search, duplicate detection, merge, CSV import, and CSV export.
Provide a chronological interaction timeline with manual email and meeting logging.
Implement saved views, filters, owner assignment, and a next-action dashboard.
Add role-based access, an immutable activity log, backups, and a recovery command.
Seed a realistic demo workspace and document field mapping for imports.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out automatic mailbox ingestion.
Deliberately leave out commercial enrichment databases.
Deliberately leave out enterprise forecasting, integrations, and compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
